articleBody:
### 📈 Anthropic starts trading in largest IPO ever

[↗ Primärquelle: theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/19/anthropic-public-trading-ipo)

- Anthropic, the maker of the Claude chatbot, began trading on the Nasdaq today after raising $81.3bn in its initial public offering, the biggest fundraise in IPO history, beating the $75bn record SpaceX set in June.
- Shares opened at $83, above last week's expected range, giving the five-year-old company a fully diluted market value of $1.5tn after it sold 980m shares to underwriters, with CEO Dario Amodei expected to ring the opening bell.
- Revenue has grown sharply, reaching $16.2bn in the first half of 2026 versus $4.6bn for all of 2025, but Anthropic lost $104bn over nine months, with compute costs of roughly $18.8bn its largest expense.

### 💥 AI-found bug fixes blamed for US outages

[↗ Primärquelle: siliconangle.com](https://siliconangle.com/2026/11/18/recent-spate-of-outages-attributed-to-technical-issues-amid-accelerated-ai-bug-discovery/)

- Wall Street executives and the NSA have told Congress that this week's US tech outages came from hurried patches for software flaws that AI models found, according to a report The Verge has not confirmed.
- The fixes briefly overwhelmed systems as banks and agencies rushed to close gaps, knowing attackers have the same AI tools; last month, Microsoft's update alone fixed about 1,400 security flaws, up from roughly 170 a year earlier.
- Since last Thursday, a Microsoft 365 outage hit email for millions, the FAA halted flights, Chase customers couldn't reach money, the NSA's classified network failed, and Apple's iCloud and Apple Pay went down.

### ⚡ Google launches Gemini 4 Neon

[↗ Primärquelle: venturebeat.com](https://venturebeat.com/technology/google-launches-gemini-4-neon-with-opus-5-5-level-coding-performance-at-25-lower-api-token-prices)

- Google has released Gemini 4 Neon, a mid-range AI model now live on its paid Gemini API, the Gemini app, and development tools, which the company says runs three times faster than its Gemini 4 Carbon model.
- Neon costs $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, about 50% more than Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol, but Google says it beats both on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its top reasoning setting.
- In coding tests the software around Neon matters: it scored 12.8% with the mini-SWE agent but 39% inside Google Antigravity, where it can split a project among several parallel Hydrogen agents, all using the same underlying model.

### 🏭 AI could double data center power use by 2030

[↗ Primärquelle: theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/19/datacentres-to-create-70-more-carbon-emissions-by-2030-iea-report-warns)

- The International Energy Agency says datacentres will use twice as much electricity by 2030 as they do today, with the worldwide spread of AI driving three-quarters of that jump in demand.
- The growth means AI datacentres will burn through an extra 350 terawatt-hours a year, more than Great Britain's yearly use, pushing the sector's carbon emissions up by 70% within four years.
- China will draw about half its datacentre power from coal by 2030, while the US leans on gas for roughly 60%, with plans for 180GW of new gas plants, nearly matching the entire EU's current gas capacity.

### ⚖️ Britain lost its fight to hide Apple backdoor order

- A UK tribunal sided with Apple, striking down the government's bid to keep secret its order demanding backdoor access to encrypted iPhone data, meaning much of the dispute will now be heard in open court.
- The Home Office issued a Technical Capability Notice that, if obeyed, would have let it reach any user's encrypted data worldwide, but the tribunal rejected its national security argument as "fanciful" since the order had already leaked widely.
- Apple refuses to build such a backdoor and has instead switched off Advanced Data Protection for UK users, leaving iPhones in Britain less protected than those anywhere else as the case against the Home Office continues.

### 🚫 TSMC and Samsung halt some China chip shipments

[↗ Primärquelle: firstpost.com](https://www.firstpost.com/tech/tsmc-and-samsung-halt-chip-shipments-to-china-following-new-us-export-curbs-report-14061331.html)

- TSMC and Samsung have stopped shipping some chips to Chinese customers after new US export rules forced them to seek licences from the Commerce Department, adding to the squeeze on China's AI industry.
- The new rules from the Bureau of Industry and Security require chipmakers using American technology to get licences, closing a path Chinese designers used to order high-performance AI chips through TSMC and Samsung.
- The change scraps earlier exemptions, so even chips meant for non-AI uses like smartphones may now need approval, hitting Samsung buyers such as Baidu's Kunlun and ByteDance and TSMC clients like Xiaomi and Oppo.

### Other news & articles you might like

- Palo Alto Networks acquires Applied Compute for $4.5 billion [↗ constellationr.com](https://www.constellationr.com/insights/news/palo-alto-networks-acquires-applied-compute-45-billion)
- Google Play wants Android apps to nail foldable basics by April 2027 [↗ 9to5google.com](https://9to5google.com/2026/11/18/android-foldable-apps-google-play/)
- Snapchat now lets developers build AR Lenses with AI assistants like Claude Code and Cursor [↗ techcrunch.com](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/18/snapchat-now-lets-developers-build-ar-lenses-with-ai-coding-assistants-like-claude-code-and-cursor/)
- Intel signs first external customer for advanced 18A chips [↗ cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/18/intel-first-18a-foundry-customer.html)
- Canva will let users switch off most generative AI [↗ engadget.com](https://www.engadget.com/2321318/canva-will-let-users-switch-off-most-generative-ai/)
- The Accelerationists Are Trying to Stop Anthropic [↗ gizmodo.com](https://gizmodo.com/the-accelerationists-are-trying-to-stop-anthropic-2000841831)
- Nvidia interim CEO Kress tells employees ‘let’s move forward’ at first all-hands meeting since Jensen Huang exit [↗ cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/18/nvidia-interim-ceo-kress-addresses-staff-after-jensen-huang-exit-.html)
- More banks says customers using AI agents are on their own — even if they get hacked [↗ techcrunch.com](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/18/more-banks-says-customers-using-ai-agents-are-on-their-own-even-if-they-get-hacked/)
- DOJ accuses Russian national of spying on and harassing Palantir employees [↗ engadget.com](https://www.engadget.com/2321489/doj-accuses-russian-national-of-spying-on-and-harassing-palantir-employees/)
- Microsoft's official Python agent framework hijacked to distribute malware [↗ theregister.com](https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/18/microsofts-official-python-agent-framework-hijacked-to-distribute-malware/5310858)
- Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explains why he asked 60K employees to quit [↗ techcrunch.com](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/18/microsoft-ceo-satya-nadella-explains-why-he-asked-60k-employees-to-quit/)
- A Tesla Model Y without a steering wheel is coming: Musk [↗ insideevs.com](https://insideevs.com/news/815960/tesla-model-y-steering-wheel-remove/)
- Moonshot drops $150M Indonesia Nvidia rental days after US loophole crackdown [↗ cryptopolitan.com](https://www.cryptopolitan.com/moonshot-drops-indonesia-nvidia-deal/)
- OpenAI says its AI found 14% gains in AMD’s flagship GPU design [↗ thenextweb.com](https://thenextweb.com/news/openai-models-amd-gpu-chip-design-14-percent)

### 🧰 Trending tools

**Hootsuite:** they asked the teams actually winning on social what is working right now and published all 17 trends in a free report, no purchase needed. Download the report

**Incredible Agents:** activate AI agents via a keyboard shortcut to see your screen, spot tasks, and complete work automatically with SOC 2 and GDPR compliance. [↗ incredible.one](https://incredible.one)

**Foolscap:** a writing app that reads your work to track characters, ideas, and loose threads, offering dialogue and AI assistance without ever writing for you. [↗ foolscap.works](https://foolscap.works)

**ExitPath:** open-source alternatives and migration guides for moving away from Slack, Notion, and Microsoft 365. [↗ exitpath-ruddy.vercel.app](https://exitpath-ruddy.vercel.app)

**Verse Engine by Ctruh:** a browser-native 3D and XR engine that converts files, scans, or Blender, Unity and Unreal exports into shareable links opening instantly without downloads. [↗ verse.ctruh.com](https://verse.ctruh.com)

**HeyGen Avatar 6:** generates professional AI avatar videos from scripts, images, or prompts in minutes, with support for 175+ languages for communicating at scale. [↗ heygen.com](https://heygen.com/models/heygen-avatar-6)

**GAtrends:** tracks your keywords across 7 sources like Google News and GitHub, learning normal levels and alerting you via Telegram when something spikes. [↗ gatrends.com](https://gatrends.com)

### 📚 Trending papers & reports

> **AirOps:** pages updated within three months are three times more likely to be cited by AI. This free guide shows how to get your brand named in AI answers. [Get the free guide](https://go.dupple.com/lg-techpresso-airops-w9ifst)

> **Personal AI assistant safety checks** vet proposed updates to an assistant's instructions before they go live, rejecting 20 of 21 risky edits and cutting policy violations to zero in one repaired case. [↗ arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23651)

> **Leaderboard rankings** can mislead buyers because the same top-rated chatbot behaves differently for different users, so the authors call for reliability claims stating whose needs are covered, under what conditions, and with what uncertainty. [↗ arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23732)

> **AI supply-chain map** catalogs how models, data, chips, capital, and talent flow between organizations, revealing the most central players, concentration, and chokepoints across the AI ecosystem. [↗ arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24927)

articleBody:
Record profits, ever-lower taxes: big tech’s tax gap is nearing €300 billion, a new study finds. Germany, Europe’s biggest market without a digital levy, is still debating whether to act.

Last year, Culture and Media Minister Wolfram Weimer promised a key-points paper on digital levies leading to a draft law. The paper has yet to appear. – Alle Rechte vorbehalten: [photothek](https://www.imago-images.de/de/st/0868917933?searchID=8e1de567-2e26-491d-a3b1-76f55a0a6dc3&isHandpicked=false&initialMediaIndex=87&totalResultsCount=3075&isPeopleFilterApplied=no&peopleFilterMode=not+applied)

Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft and Netflix dominate the global digital infrastructure. The so-called Silicon Six are earning jaw-dropping profits, but the share they pay in taxes keeps shrinking.

At the same time, the tax gap is widening. This is the amount countries would have collected in taxes if profits had been taxed in the countries where they were earned. [The Fair Tax Foundation](https://fairtaxmark.net/the-silicon-six-300bn-global-tax-gap/), a British NGO, puts the gap over the last decade at €278 billion ($316.7 billion). A third of that is in Europe alone.

## Taxed like a tax haven

The Silicon Six’s profits have skyrocketed in the last decade, and their market value shows it. Today, they are worth 1.5 times the market capitalization of Europe’s 150 largest listed companies combined.

Meanwhile, these big tech companies benefit from substantial tax breaks. The Fair Tax Foundation details these breaks in a new [report](https://fairtaxmark.net/wp-content/uploads/Silicon-Six-Report-2026.pdf).

Combined, the Silicon Six have generated over $13 trillion in revenue and $3.3 trillion of profits over the past ten years. Their average income tax rate over the same period was 16.5%, well below the global average of 26.6%, according to the report.

Much of the tax relief is linked to [US President Donald Trump’s 2017 tax reform](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/BILLS-115hr1ih/). Among other things, the breaks favored foreign-derived income, cutting its tax rate by nearly 40%.

Furthermore, [generous US write-offs on investment in data centers](https://news.bgov.com/daily-tax-report/data-center-spenders-save-billions-from-depreciation-tax-break) have deepened the shortfall in recent years. The report says the six companies’ tax rate dropped to 12.3% in 2025. Meta and Amazon paid less than 9%. That puts their global tax rate at the level of a tax haven. The authors expect this rate to continue to fall in 2026.

The US is not the only refuge. Booking profits in so-called hub countries is another avoidance practice. Even within the EU, multinational groups can pay a substantial share of their European taxes in a single low-tax hub country, rather than in the individual markets where their customers are based.

That is why many tech companies from outside the EU have set up in Ireland. According to the report, Apple and Microsoft declared around 90% of their EU taxes in Ireland in 2025. Their subsidiaries in other EU member states reported far less taxable income. Ireland’s corporate tax rates have historically been less than half of Germany’s.

“In the interest of fair competition, stable tax revenue and economic independence, the German government and the EU must no longer tolerate this tax privilege, which distorts competition,” said Christoph Trautvetter, managing director of the Tax Justice Network Germany (Netzwerk Steuergerechtigkeit), commenting on the report.

## What happened to Germany’s digital levy?

The figures in Germany are particularly striking. [A calculation published in May by the Tax Justice Network](https://www.netzwerk-steuergerechtigkeit.de/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/260624_JB_online.pdf)shows that Microsoft, Apple, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta paid an effective tax rate of 3.2% in 2025. The country’s tax rate is roughly 30%.

Yet Germany is still the largest European market for tech companies without a digital levy. The UK, France, Spain, Italy and Austria all charge some form of levy. In Austria, for example, large online platforms have paid 5% of their advertising revenue since 2020.

[Berlin has promised to act](https://netzpolitik.org/2025/digitalsteuer-tech-konzerne-sollen-blechen/). The coalition agreement commits the government to examining a digital tax, but the deadlines keep slipping. Last year, Culture and Media Minister Wolfram Weimer said he would present a key-points paper ahead of a bill in late 2025. A year later, the paper has yet to appear.

Weimer has floated a rate of around 10%, which he calls a “Plattform-Soli.” Revenues are expected to reach billions of euros. But the coalition is divided over the design. “The Social Democrats want a classic digital tax model, the CSU would rather have nothing at all,” [Weimer said](https://www.boersennews.de/nachrichten/artikel/dpa-afx/weimer-koalition-ringt-weiter-um-digitalabgabe/5117319/).

articleBody:
[Dan Larson](https://www.instagram.com/toygalaxy/) of [Secret Galaxy](https://www.youtube.com/@SecretGalaxyTV) explained how [General Mills](https://www.generalmills.com/) transformed breakfast cereals in the 1970s by introducing [iconic monster-themed cereals](https://laughingsquid.com/monster-cereal-commercials-through-the-years/), such as Count Chocula, Franken Berry, and Boo Berry, that entertained rather than frightened children. He also explored the full history of these cereals, from their wonderful animated commercials to unexpected health controversies, plus subsequent toys, records, snacks and other product licensing that helped cement each character’s legacy.

> The monster cereals are a line of breakfast cereals produced by General Mills Corporation in North America. The line was introduced in 1971, and at various times has included five brands, each featuring a cartoon version of a classic movie monster: Count Chocula, Franken Berry, and Boo Berry, as well as Fruit Brute and Fruity Yummy Mummy.

The monsters have kept getting makeovers since, and [according to General Mills](https://www.generalmills.com/news/stories/the-history-of-our-monsters), [Jim Henson’s Creature Shop](https://www.creatureshop.com/) turned Count Chocula, Franken Berry, and Boo Berry into puppets in 2025 for The Jim Henson Company’s 70th anniversary.

> [Monster Cereal Commercials Through the Years](https://laughingsquid.com/monster-cereal-commercials-through-the-years/)

title: Frieze Abu Dhabi Debuts to Brisk Sales and Confident Dealers
subtitle: On the morning of Frieze Abu Dhabi’s inaugural edition, Saudi Arabia’s financial center in Riyadh was reportedly attacked by Yemen’s Iran-backed Ho…
feedText: The crowd in Abu Dhabi, at least, had other things on their minds: the fair was about to open, with millions of dollars’ worth of art ready to be sold. Members of the royal family were back after getting a sneak peek yesterday, alongside politicians and celebrities including tennis star Venus Williams and architect Kulapat Yantrasast. “It’s about time. Frieze is bringing its A-game to Abu Dhabi, where they have the best museums,” Yantrasast told ARTnews, cheekily mentioning that he’s been putting dots on artwork…
articleBody:
On the morning of Frieze Abu Dhabi’s inaugural edition, Saudi Arabia’s financial center in Riyadh was reportedly attacked by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels. The crowd in Abu Dhabi, at least, had other things on their minds: the fair was about to open, with millions of dollars’ worth of art ready to be sold. Members of the royal family were back after getting a sneak peek yesterday, alongside politicians and celebrities including tennis star Venus Williams and architect Kulapat Yantrasast.

“It’s about time. Frieze is bringing its A-game to Abu Dhabi, where they have the best museums,” Yantrasast told *ARTnews*, cheekily mentioning that he’s been putting dots on artworks from The Third Line, Taymour Grahne Projects, Experimenter and Pearl Lam Projects.

The dealers were in high spirits too, as booths started to get busy an hour after the opening. At Thaddeus Ropac, three of Imran Qureshi’s *Water Bodies* sold for $60,000, each to a UAE-based collection, though the gallery declined to specify whether this was a private or institutional collection.

“There is a great energy around the fair in Abu Dhabi this week. We’re having good conversations with collectors who are well-informed about the artists we are presenting, and you can feel the impact of the institutional scene here,” Xenia Geroulanos, director at Thaddaeus Ropac, told *ARTnews*.

Venus Williams at ArtAncient’s booth at Frieze Abu Dhabi 2026.

ARTnews

The fair is under the umbrella of Frieze and has rebranded from Abu Dhabi Art fair, and attendees are noticing a difference. The exhibitor list has been streamlined to 89, down from 142 last year. Dealer Asmaa Al-Shabibi told *ARTnews* that when she walked through the fair’s new entrance, it felt “a little bit like going into Frieze London, and it feels like a different fair.”

Samy Ghiyati, co-founder of art advisory NG Partners, agreed. “The quality is definitely higher, and galleries made an effort to bring very good inventory. Usually fairs in the region are slower and sales happen over the course of several days,” he told *ARTnews*.

One of Ghiyati’s clients placed three orders on pieces ranging from $10,000 to $400,000. Within an hour of opening, dealer Sundaram Tagore had already placed two works on hold, one by Hiroshi Senju and another by Chun Kwang Young, ranging from $40,000 to $400,000. By late afternoon, Timothy Taylor had sold its entire solo presentation of paintings by Hilary Pecis to institutional and private collections in the region and internationally, to the price of $65,000-$205,000. The London-based antiquities gallery David Aaron sold a 2,000-year-old funerary stele for a seven-figure sum to a private collector, while Dubai-based Taymour Grahne Projects also sold out its booth of mosaic works depicting 70s-era architecture in Abu Dhabi.

Regional collectors reportedly spent big at Frieze Abu Dhabi. Iris Projects sold two works by Shamsa Al Omaira, a sculpture acquired by a new foundation in the UAE for $32,000 and an acrylic on canvas by Juma Al Haj for $20,400. UAE-based collectors also bought two ceramics by Eman Al Hashemi, priced at $17,000 and $15,000, an oil pastel on linen by Dhabia Al Qubaisi for $10,500, and a photograph by Ammar Al Attar for $12,500.

Rayan Ben El Mlih, sales and marketing manager at Waddington Custot, told *ARTnews* that a large contingent of collectors with reserves hailed from Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Qatar and Bahrain. The gallery brought works by Etel Adnan, Sophia Vari and Fabienne Verdier.

Galleria Continua’s booth at Frieze Abu Dhabi, 2026. The booth featured works by Anish Kapoor, Barbana Bojadzi, and Hank Willis Thomas, priced between $5,500 and $823,000 (€5,000 to €750,000).

Courtesy Nino Consorte/Frieze

Dealers noted that local collectors, some of whom began their collections by acquiring Western artists, are now deepening their collections with more historical pieces by regional artists.

“We’ve been seeing European collectors diversifying their collections, too,” said Ghiyati. Dubai’s Carbon 12 sold a painting and a sculpture by 28-year-old artist Sarah Al Mehairi, as well as two works by Mexican artist Edgar Orlaineta, priced between $17,570 and $35,000 (€16,000-€32,000).

“We’ve engaged mostly with collectors that we’ve cultivated relationships with for a while, and this is our home fair,” Judy Karkour, associate director of Carbon 12, told *ARTnews*.

Collectors are branching out beyond SWANA this year, with notable interest in art from the African continent and its diaspora and Latin America. Meanwhile this year’s Frieze Masters section is dedicated to trade across the Indian Ocean, taking its cues from the Louvre Abu Dhabi’s current exhibition “Spices and Wonders: Sailing the Indian Ocean.” An hour into the fair, Efie Gallery had placed two works by Malian artist Abdoulaye Konaté on reserve, both priced between $45,000 to $65,000, in addition to two works by Cuban artist Maria Magdalena Campos Pons ($27,500-$55,000).

“Frieze Abu Dhabi has got off to a strong start for us with a high volume of enquiries in the first few hours from both institutions and private collections,” Kwame Mintah, cofounder of Efie Gallery, told *ARTnews*, which specializing in artists of African descent. “One of the more encouraging developments across the Gulf has been the gradual maturation of its collecting community, accompanied by a growing appreciation for artistic practices beyond established geographical and institutional frameworks,” he added.

At Daniel Crouch Rare Books, a private collector bought the first map to name Abu Dhabi, dated to 1832. While dealer Daniel Crouch declined to say how much the map sold for, he priced the booth’s total value between $10,073 and $1.19 million (AED 37,000 to AED 4.4 million).

“Abu Dhabi is becoming a cultural hub in the region with a lot of development,” Crouch said. “It’s the logical place to come to for dealing in the larger Indian Ocean region and the Louvre Abu Dhabi exhibition has attracted quite a lot of attention—we’ve obviously jumped into it with alacrity.” London-based antiquities gallery ArtAncient, carrying pieces ranging from $5,000 to $5 million, sold a collection of shipwreck jewels for an undisclosed sum—the gallery also had a visit from Venus Williams, who was admiring the Graeco-Roman mummy portrait *Portrait L*, which had recently been dubbed the “[Mona Lisa of the Middle East](https://www.thetimes.com/culture/art/article/the-mona-lisa-of-the-middle-east-that-inspired-the-picture-of-dorian-grey-ns92lqskj).”

Throughout the opening, the blue-chip-leaning powerhouses, including Gagosian, Pace Gallery, Thaddaeus Ropac, and Victoria Miro, boasted crowded booths. Gagosian’s dedicated Roy Lichtenstein booth became the step and repeat for many visitors—the gallery said it “placed many” orders without revealing specifics.

Gagosian’s booth at Frieze Abu Dhabi 2026, featuring Roy Lichtenstein.

Ismail Noor

Judging by its debut, Abu Dhabi has become a no-brainer stop on the art fair calendar. The emirate is slowly integrating into the art circuit. Earlier this month, Christie’s hosted its first fine art auction there, with Sotheby’s own version due next month, joining a colorful lineup of events that includes the Formula 1 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, Abu Dhabi Finance Week and Culture Summit Abu Dhabi.

Several dealers cited the Guggenheim Abu Dhabi’s upcoming December opening with the strong pull to participate in Frieze Abu Dhabi, characterizing the museum as a bridge between West and East.

“The Guggenheim is going to open now in the next few weeks, it’s literally where contemporary art gets space to breathe and to grow,” said Milo Gatti, fair coordinator at Galleria Continua.

articleBody:
**Heute ist es ja schon lange kein Problem mehr, professionell Musik ausschließlich am Rechner zu produzieren. Laptop-Producer können das sogar überall machen: Auf dem Sofa, in der Bahn oder im Flugzeug, im Hotelzimmer oder in einem anderen Studio. Was brauchst du neben dem Rechner wirklich, um überall passend ausgerüstet zu sein?**

## Inhalt:

- Essentials für mobile Laptop-Producer
- beyerdynamic DT 700 PRO X: Verlässlicher Studiokopfhörer für Laptop-Producer
- Studio-Sound für mobile Laptop-Producer: IK Multimedia ARC ON·EAR

## Essentials für mobile Laptop-Producer

Musik ausschließlich am Laptop zu produzieren ist eigentlich nichts besonderes mehr. Rechner bringen genug Leistung mit, um „in-the-box“ Musik zu komponieren, zu arrangieren, abzumischen und zu mastern. Viele heutige Hits sind komplett am Rechner entstanden und wurden vielleicht sogar auf einem Laptop in einem Hotelzimmer produziert. Selbst wenn „Laptop-Producer“ nicht unbedingt deine Präferenz ist, ist es manchmal einfach auch bequem, unterwegs oder auf dem Sofa an musikalischen Projekten zu arbeiten.

Neben einem Laptop und einer DAW gibt es zusätzliches Gear, das für Laptop-Producer nützlich ist. Ein Kopfhörer steht da natürlich ganz oben auf der Liste, aber da gibt‘s noch ein paar Sachen, die ein Setup sinnvoll ergänzen. Wir wollen dir ein paar Produkte vorstellen, stellvertretend für die Essentials.

## beyerdynamic DT 700 PRO X: Verlässlicher Studiokopfhörer für Laptop-Producer

beyerdynamic DT 700 PRO X Kopfhörer · Quelle: beyerdynamic

Wer am Laptop Musik produziert und abmischt, braucht natürlich eine Abhöre. Stationär werden [Studiomonitore](https://www.gearnews.de/tag/studiomonitor/) wohl die erste Wahl sein – aber wir stellen uns vor, dass du als Laptop-Producer gerne auch mobil arbeitest. Und da sind Kopfhörer gefragt.

Vielleicht hast du dich schon mal mit dem Thema beschäftigt und gesehen, wie viele gute Studiokopfhörer es gibt. Deshalb ist die Wahl nicht einfach. Wir haben einen kleinen [Kaufberater](https://www.gearnews.de/kopfhoerer-studio-recording-mixing-producing/) am Start, der einige Modelle empfehlt. Vielleicht findest du da direkt einen Kopfhörer, der genau richtig für dich ist.

Wir zeigen dir den **DT 700 PRO X**, ein noch ziemlicher neuer Kopfhörer aus der Pro-X-Reihe des deutschen Herstellers beyerdynamic. Die Serie zeichnet sich durch die weiterntwickelten Stellar.45-Treiber aus, zudem wurde an dem Tragekomfort gefeilt. Gegenüber älteren Modellen überzeugt der Kopfhörer auch durch das austauschbare und einseitig geführte Kabel – zwei davon gehören inklusive Klinkenadapter und Transporttasche zum Lieferumfang. Und auch die Ohr- und Kopfpolster lassen sich hier austauschen!

DT 700 PRO X ist ein geschlossener und ohrumschließender Kopfhörer, der einen Übertragungsbereich von 5 Hz bis 40 kHz abdeckt. Geschlossene Kopfhörer isolieren dich besser von der Außenwelt, einige bevorzugen beim Abmischen aber Modelle mit offener Bauweise wie beispielsweise [DT 900 Pro X](https://www.thomann.de/de/beyerdynamic_dt_900_pro_x.htm?offid=1&affid=84)* (um bei beyerdynamic zu bleiben). In dem Sinne ist deine Entscheidung auch eine Frage des persönlichen Geschmacks. DT 700 PRO X beyerdynamic DT 700 PRO X bekommst du [bei Thomann](https://www.thomann.de/de/beyerdynamic_dt_700_pro_x.htm?offid=1&affid=84)*.

## Studio-Sound für mobile Laptop-Producer: IK Multimedia ARC ON·EAR

Du besitzt einen Laptop und hast darauf eine DAW installiert, einen Kopfhörer besitzt du ebenfalls (oder hast schon einen auf der Wunschliste). Nun möchten wir dir eine aus unserer Sicht gute Ergänzung dafür vorstellen.

**ARC ON·EAR** von IK Multimedia ist sehr neues System, mit dem du die Möglichkeiten deines Kopfhörers erweiterst. Es handelt sich nämlich um ein kleines, tragbares Standalone-Kopfhörer-Korrektursystem. Das ist mit einem DAC (also einem Wandler) und einem Kpüfhörerverstärker in Studioqualität ausgestattet. Der Kniff ist hier, dass du mit dieser kleinen Box die Frequenzantwort deines Kopfhörers korrigierst und sogar Studioumgebungen mit professionellen Monitorlautsprechern simulieren kannst.

Nicht nur für Laptop-Producer praktisch: IK Multimedia ARC ON·EAR · Quelle: IK Multimedia

Über die zugehörige Software passt du ARC ON·EAR nach deinen Bedürfnissen an und erstellst bis zu fünf benutzerdefinierte Profile, die sich auf ARC ON·EAR laden lassen. Zu den simulierten Umgebungen gehören mehr als 20 bekannte Studiomonitore und 15 Wiedergabesysteme. Praktisch ist, dass hier nicht nur ein USB-C-Anschluss für die Verbindung zum Rechner und zum Aufladen dran ist, sondern auch ein analoger Audioeingang. Der Einsatz dieses Tools ist also in den unterschiedlichsten Setups denkbar.

ARC ON·EAR ist natürlich nicht nur für Laptop-Producer interessant, sondern generell für alle, die oft und gerne mit Kopfhörern produzieren und abmischen. In unserem kleinen [Testbericht](https://www.gearnews.de/arc-on-ear-ik-multimedia-recording/) kannst du mehr über das System herausfinden. ARC ON·EAR bekommst du [hier bei Thomann](https://www.thomann.de/de/ik_multimedia_arc_onear.htm?offid=1&affid=84)*.

## Ein kleines und kompaktes Audiointerface ermöglicht überall Aufnahmen

Vielleicht ist dir wichtig, überall für eine Aufnahme gewappnet zu sein. Genau für so eine Aufgabe ist ein kleines Audiointerface gedacht. Selbst wenn du ein festes Studio-Setup besitzt, kann ein zusätzliches kompaktes Audiointerface eine sehr sinnvolle Anschaffung sein. Denn meistens ist das Equipment im Studio fest verkabelt und da hast du vielleicht nicht immer Lust, da für einen kleinen Trip oder die Session in einer anderen Umgebung rangehen zu müssen.

Aus diesem Grund muss das kleine Interface auch gar nicht unbedingt mit vielen üppigen Funktionen ausgestattet sein. Auf ein paar Aspekte würde ich aber trotzdem immer achten: Eigenen sich die Eingänge für den Anschluss von Mikrofonen über XLR und können die Mikros mit Phantomspeisung versorgt werden? Sind zwei Line-taugliche Eingänge dran, um Stereoaufnahmen zu machen? Und kann ich auch Instrumente anschließen?

Praktisch für Laptop-Producer ist auch, wenn ein Kopfhörer angeschlossen werden kann. Dann ist eine Hardware wie das gerade gezeigte ARC ON·EAR zum Beispiel primär ein cooles Add-on.

Audient EVO 4 erfüllt alle hier angesprochenen Anforderungen und bietet zudem noch einige sehr nützliche Funktionen. Dazu zählen der Smartgain-Modus für das automatische Aussteuern von Signalen oder Loopback für Streaming oder Podcast-Aufnahmen.

Das Interface ist mit einem USB-C-Anschluss ausgerüstet und funktioniert mit MAC, Windows und iOS sogar ClassCompliant. Das alles verpackt EVO 4 in einem kleinen und leichten Format. [Hier bei Thomann](https://www.thomann.de/de/audient_evo_4.htm?offid=1&affid=84)* kannst du dir das Interface einmal genauer anschauen.

## Was fehlt? Ein Controller vielleicht?

Kompakte Controller wie Arturia MiniLab 3 sind für Laptop-Producer eine perfekte Ergänzung · Quelle: Arturia

Runden wir das Setup für Laptop-Producer ab. „In-the-box“ ist ja im Prinzip alles möglich und in der Theorie kannst du mit Trackpad und Tastatur so ziemlich jede Aufgabe in der DAW bewerkstelligen. Aber in der Praxis macht es manchmal auch einfach mehr Spaß, mit einem Controller zu arbeiten. Zu diesem Thema haben wir direkt zwei schöne Kaufberater parat:

- [Die besten Keyboard-Controller zur DAW-Steuerung](https://www.gearnews.de/die-besten-usb-midi-keyboard-controller-zur-daw-steuerung/)
- [Die besten](https://www.gearnews.de/die-besten-usb-keyboard-controller-fuer-unterwegs/)[USB-Keyboard-Controller für unterwegs](https://www.gearnews.de/die-besten-usb-keyboard-controller-fuer-unterwegs/)

In beide solltest du mal reinlesen, um vielleicht auch ein Gefühl dafür zu bekommen, was für dich wichtig ist. Und es ist auch gar nicht so einfach, einen einzelnen Controller für dieses Perfect Match auszuwählen. Gehen wir mal davon aus, dass es ein kleines Modell sein soll. Denn einen „Backpack-Controller“ kannst du überall hin mitnehmen und auch überall bequem aufbauen. Aber was ist dir dabei wichtig? Eine paar Keys zum Einspielen, Pads für das Triggern von Drums, Regler für Modulationen, Fader für schnelle Änderungen der Paramteter? Oder vielleicht von allem ein bisschen?

**Arturia MiniLab 3** erfüllt diese Anforderungen, deshalb stellen wir dir dieses Modell als Beispiel für einen flexiblen Controller vor. Hier sind 25 Slim-Keys dran, die sogar auf die Anschlagstärke reagieren. Das wird mit acht kleinen Pads, acht Drehreglern und vier Fadern ergänzt.

An der Rückseite kannst du sogar ein Pedal für Expression oder Sustain anschließen. Und zwei Touchstrips eignen sich für Pitchbend und Modulation. Zusätzlich ist hier ein ganz schönes Software-Paket dabei. Und nicht ganz unwichtig: es gibt mehrere Farbvarianten – ganz neu ist Champagner! Arturia MiniLab 3 bekommst du [bei Thomann](https://www.thomann.de/de/search_AR_627252_553721_553717.html?offid=1&affid=84)*.

## Fazit

Du bist als Laptop-Producer bereits mit einem Laptop und deiner Lieblings-DAW ausgerüstet. Eine gute Ergänzung in Hinblick auf mobiles Producing ist auf jeden Fall ein Kopfhörer. Ein verlässliches Modell in geschlossener Bauweise ist der beyerdynamic DT 700 PRO X.

Ergänzend ist ein System wie IK Multimedia ARC ON·EAR eine sehr interessante Option, denn hiermit erweiterst du die Möglichkeiten deines Kopfhörers und mischt mit dem Sound wie in einem Studioraum. Zudem erhältst du hiermit weitere Simulationen verschiedener Hörumgebungen und die Simulation von unterschiedlichen Kopfhörermodellen.

Wer unterwegs auch jederzeit für eine Aufnahme ausgerüstet sein möchte, kommt um ein kleines Audiointerface nicht herum. Als gutes Beispiel zeigen wir dir das Audient Evo 4. Hier sind die wichtigsten Anschlüsse dran, um professionelle Mikrofone, Instrumente wie eine E-Gitarre und auch Line-Quellen wie Synthesizer, Drum-Machines oder den Stereoausgang eines Mixers anzuschließen. Gepaart mit ein paar nützlichen Funktionen hast du damit bereits die Basis für ein mobiles Laptop-Studio.

Und auch ein kompakter Controller wie Arturia MiniLab 3 ist eine Überlegung wert, denn hiermit kannst du überall mal eine Melodie, eine Bassline und ein paar Akkorde einspielen oder auf Drum-Pads jammen, Modulationen mit Reglern aufnehmen und einige weitere Aufgaben erledigen.

Zusammen ist dieses Gear aus unserer Sicht ein Perfect Match für Laptop-Producer.

title: Six Factors That Support Mental Health for Black Youth
subtitle: On a summer day at UC Berkeley, four teenagers jostled at a whiteboard, vying to write down their solutions to an important public health concern.
feedText: They were having fun even as they took on a heavy task: helping researchers design programs to reduce the skyrocketing suicide rate among Black youth. In the United States, deaths by suicide have been surging among Black kids and teens for decades. For those between 10 and 17 years of age, the suicide rate rose 144% from 2007 to 2020. articleBody:
On a summer day at UC Berkeley, four teenagers jostled at a whiteboard, vying to write down their solutions to an important public health concern. They were having fun even as they took on a heavy task: helping researchers design programs to reduce the skyrocketing suicide rate among Black youth.

In the United States, deaths by suicide have been surging among Black kids and teens for decades. For those between 10 and 17 years of age, the suicide rate [rose 144% from 2007 to 2020](https://publichealth.jhu.edu/sites/default/files/2023-08/2023-august-still-ringing-alarm.pdf). What’s more, Black boys die by suicide more than twice as frequently as Black girls, although the suicide rate for Black girls [increased by 182% between 2001 and 2017](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10900-019-00678-x).

As the teenagers brainstormed, [Jasmin Brooks Stephens](https://psychology.berkeley.edu/people/jasmin-brooks-stephens), a Berkeley assistant professor of psychology, watched nearby. The moment was a highlight in research she was conducting with the Homeless Children’s Network on improving mental health outcomes for Black youth. Brooks Stephens believed that teens themselves have meaningful ideas to share, and she had worked for eight weeks with these particular teenagers, who were part of the network’s [Jabali Youth Advocacy](https://www.hcnkids.org/jabali-youth-advocacy) organization, culminating in their trip to campus.

“One of the most exciting things was seeing them all jump up and say, ‘Wait, we can make a program for making us feel better? We have the power to do that?’” Brooks Stephens recalled. “Seeing them find and discover that sense of agency in themselves—that was invaluable to me.” It also was one of the few times any of the teens had visited a college campus, she said, an added bonus. In future work, Brooks Stephens plans to translate the results of her study for clinicians and policymakers who are trying to improve suicide prevention for Black youth.

The ongoing project is just one example of how Brooks Stephens is working to address rising suicide rates among Black youth by engaging them in participatory research—an unusual and hopeful approach in suicide prevention studies. “This summer I had the incredible opportunity to work alongside young people to design a program that would help other young people want to live,” she said. “Rather than waiting until a young person is already in crisis, I’m interested in understanding what helps youth thrive—what gives them hope and a sense of possibility and helps them recognize the brilliance they have inside them.”

## A pathway to hope in the face of racism

Despite the growing crisis among Black youth, [suicide rates are dropping for adolescents in the U.S. overall](https://www.samhsa.gov/data/sites/default/files/reports/rpt57150/2025-nsduh-annual-national-report.pdf). Brooks Stephens finds these statistics revealing: “To me, that suggests that the approaches we have relied on have not adequately addressed the conditions driving suicide risk in Black communities,” she said.

It’s easy to talk about [structural racism](https://news.berkeley.edu/2025/08/14/watch-berkeley-scholar-explain-structural-racism/) as an abstract concept, or personal encounters with racists as disturbing but bounded moments. But grappling with racism heavily impacts Black youth and increases their suicide risk, according to a 2023 report from the [Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health](https://publichealth.jhu.edu/sites/default/files/2023-08/2023-august-still-ringing-alarm.pdf). Indeed, Brooks Stephens has published work documenting how racial discrimination and the COVID-19 pandemic, which disproportionately harmed Black Americans, together [worsened suicide risk for Black young adults](https://psycnet.apa.org/record/2025-01327-001).

Brooks Stephens’s work is informed by both her research and her own experience of how race can shape young people’s sense of self. “I became aware very early on that Black children are often navigating expectations about who they are supposed to be before they have even had the opportunity to figure out who they are for themselves,” she said. “That has stayed with me—the importance of creating space for Black young people to define themselves, recognize their strengths, and imagine who they want to become.” At the same time, she saw how the stigma surrounding mental health could make it harder for Black youth and families to seek support, even as racism and other chronic stressors were impacting their well-being.

When she took an African American psychology class as an undergraduate at the University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill, with Enrique Neblett, a renowned scholar of race and health who became her mentor, Brooks Stephens saw the connection between those experiences—and found her passion. “I realized that there was an entire field devoted to understanding how racism affects mental health and how Black children come to understand themselves and their racial identity,” she said.

Later, during her doctoral research at the University of Houston, Brooks Stephens worked with Rheeda Walker, an expert on suicide science and African American adult mental health research. Brooks Stephens noticed that there was very limited discussion about building upstream resilience in suicide prevention research—an approach that focuses on child well-being and happiness before the development of a mental health crisis.

“We’re studying why people choose to end their life without understanding what makes people want to live,” she said. For Brooks Stephens, that realization opened up a different way of thinking about suicide prevention, one that made room for the strengths that were often absent from traditional models, such as racial identity, spirituality, family connection, belonging, or hope.

## Focusing on strengths to prevent suicide

Brooks Stephens knows she can’t single-handedly eliminate the racial traumas faced by young Black people. Nor can she end other factors that lead to higher suicide rates in her community, such as systemic injustice or poverty. Instead, she’s focusing on where she can make a difference through her research.

“While I may not be able to eradicate racism, I can help build programs that change how Black young people see themselves and their futures—programs that help them feel grounded in their identity and able to imagine a life that feels worth living,” she said.

*Brooks Stephens and her colleagues identified six positive factors that reduce suicidality among Black youth (courtesy of Jasmin Brooks Stephens).*

As a first step, this year she and her colleagues created the [Black Youth Thriving Framework for Suicide Prevention](https://psycnet.apa.org/record/2027-42684-001). It’s based on a literature review that identified six protective factors that can reduce suicidality among Black youth, including family support, community ties, and self-acceptance. “What we’re working to identify now are the strategies that can help cultivate those strengths in young people’s lives,” Brooks Stephens said.

Already, in a [study from 2023](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/00957984211037440), she and her colleagues showed that Black young adults with stronger feelings of self-acceptance are less vulnerable to depression and suicide. Likewise, she has identified [mindfulness and meditation as potential tools](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12671-023-02180-x) for Black Americans in their early 20s to buffer the impulsivity that is often associated with suicide risk.

This approach is a radical departure from the status quo. Right now, resources for preventing suicide orbit around moments of crisis, Brooks Stephens said. When a child shows signs of depression or arrives at a hospital following a suicide attempt, that’s when an intervention is often provided. Brooks Stephens wants to develop research-backed ways to prevent a child from ever getting to that troubling point in the first place.

And, increasingly, she is asking Black young people themselves to help determine what those approaches should look like. Brooks Stephens said that the four teens with whom she worked this summer were not simply research participants; they were collaborators in imagining what suicide prevention could become.

“It’s very uplifting for me because I’m bringing underserved voices into our research and I’m designing solutions,” she said. “And those solutions are how we make kids want to live and love themselves. That’s it. It’s loving themselves, loving their life. That’s what I’m helping them discover.”

This article was originally published on [Berkeley News](https://news.berkeley.edu). Read the [original article](https://news.berkeley.edu/2026/10/07/as-the-suicide-rate-grows-among-black-youth-heres-where-a-berkeley-researcher-sees-reason-for-hope/).
